transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm not wasting your time with this, I really do. It's just... well, it's about this scar on my wrist. 

I know it's probably not as bad as it looks to me, I try to be rational and tell myself that. But... when I’m at church, or when I sit down to play bridge with the girls, I just keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to it. It feels like it’s the very first thing they notice about me now. 

I know that probably sounds a bit silly for a woman my age to fuss over, doesn't it? I really don't want to seem vain, but it's just been making me so terribly uncomfortable lately, if that makes sense?
Is it just the scar on your wrist that you feel self-conscious about, or are there other parts of your body that bother you as well?

Oh, no, no, it's really just the scar. I mean, at my age, you know, things shift and change, and I suppose we all get a few more wrinkles than we'd like. But I've always been quite sensible about all that. It's just this one particular thing that seems to have... gotten stuck in my head, I suppose. 

I don't sit around analyzing every little flaw, I promise. I try to keep myself busy with my bookkeeping work and my social groups. It's just the wrist. Does that seem normal to you? To just be bothered by this one specific thing?
Has this concern about the scar on your wrist been interfering with your daily activities or sleep?

Well, I... I suppose it has a little bit, maybe more than I'd like to admit. I really try not to let it get in the way of things, I promise I do. I'm usually very dependable! 

But lately, I... well, I've actually been a bit late turning in some of my bookkeeping work. I just get so caught up trying to find the right long-sleeved blouse, or positioning my watch just so, you know, to make sure it won't be noticed. And... I've even skipped a few of my choir practices and theater volunteer days. I just couldn't bear the thought of sitting there, feeling like everyone was staring at it while I was trying to hold my music or hand out programs. 

I know that sounds terrible, doesn't it? Missing my commitments over something so silly. I really am trying to do better, I just... I get so flustered. Do you think that's awful of me to let it affect my responsibilities like that?
Do you think your concern about the scar is proportionate to how noticeable it actually is to others?

Well, I... I try to tell myself it isn't, I really do. I know I'm probably making a mountain out of a molehill, and I'm sure most people wouldn't even look twice if they passed me on the street. I know that, logically. 

But... oh, it's just so hard to explain without sounding completely foolish. When I'm sitting down, say, playing bridge with the ladies or at church, and my hands are right there on the table or holding a hymnal... I just can't shake this awful feeling that their eyes are going right to it. It just feels like it's the very first thing they see when they look at me, even if they're too polite to say anything. 

I know it's probably not nearly as noticeable as my mind makes it out to be. I really am trying to be sensible about it. Does that make any sense at all? I hope you don't think I'm just being terribly vain.
Is your main concern about the scar that it looks unattractive or that it might lead others to ask you about it?

Oh, goodness... I'm not entirely sure, to be perfectly honest. I suppose I haven't really separated the two in my head. I mean, I do worry that it looks... well, unsightly. I've always taken a lot of pride in presenting myself neatly, especially when I'm handling people's accounts or volunteering. So, feeling like there's this ugly mark right out in the open, it just makes me feel very self-conscious. 

But then... oh, the thought of someone actually pointing it out or asking me about it... I think I'd just be mortified. I wouldn't know what to say, and I'd absolutely hate to make a fuss or make anyone else feel awkward for asking. I really just want to be pleasant and not draw any negative attention to myself. 

So I guess it's a bit of both? I'm sorry, I don't know if that's the exact answer you were looking for. I hope I'm explaining this properly for you. Does that make sense, or am I just not being very clear?
Is it more the appearance of the scar itself that bothers you, or the thought of what others might think if they see it?

Oh, I... I suppose that's quite close to what we were just saying, isn't it? I hope I'm not frustrating you by not having a simple 'either-or' answer ready. I really am trying to think it through for you. 

I think... well, maybe it's mostly what they might think of me. I'd just absolutely hate for anyone to look at my wrist and think I'm careless or... or unkempt, especially at my age and in my line of work. People expect a bookkeeper to be very precise and tidy, you know? But then, I suppose if the scar didn't look so... so flawed to me in the first place, I wouldn't be worrying about their thoughts at all. 

Oh dear, I'm just talking in circles now, aren't I? I'm so sorry, I really don't mean to be confusing. I promise I'm trying my best to give you a good answer. Is that alright, or do you need me to try and be a bit more specific for your notes?
Is it the fear of people noticing the scar itself that bothers you, or the fear of them asking you questions about how you got it?

Oh dear... I feel terrible, you're having to ask me this in so many different ways. I must be doing a dreadful job of explaining myself, and I'm so sorry for being so confusing. I really don't mean to test your patience.

To be perfectly honest... I haven't really thought about them asking *how* I got it. I don't think it's the story behind the scar that worries me at all. It's just... well, if they ask a question, any question really, it just confirms that they've been looking right at it. And that's the part that makes me feel so terribly uncomfortable. 

I hope I'm finally giving you the right answer. I really am trying to be helpful and give you what you need for your evaluation. Am I making a bit more sense this time, or did I miss the mark again?
Is it the appearance of the scar itself that you think is drawing people's attention, or is it just that it's something different about you that might make them look?

Oh, I see what you're asking now. I'm sorry, I'm probably making this much harder than it needs to be, aren't I? 

I suppose... well, I know the scar on my wrist is probably not as bad as it looks to me. I try to tell myself that, anyway. But when I’m out and about, especially at church or when I'm playing bridge with the ladies, I just keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to it. It feels like it's the very first thing they notice about me now, just because of how it looks. It's so silly of me to worry about it at my age, I know. 

I hope that answers your question a bit better? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you think people would notice the scar as much if it were in a less conspicuous location on your body?

Oh, goodness, that's... that's a very good question. I'm sorry, I should have thought of that myself, shouldn't I? 

I suppose if it were somewhere else... like on my stomach or my back, well, no one would ever see it, would they? I wouldn't have to worry at all. But because it's right here on my wrist, where my sleeve rides up when I'm reaching for a ledger or passing a cup of tea... it just feels so exposed. 

If it were somewhere hidden, I don't think I'd be taking up your valuable time talking about it. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for. I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how silly I'm being about this whole thing.
Do you think you would still be bothered by the scar if you were certain that no one else noticed it?

Oh, my... well, that's something to think about, isn't it? I'm sorry, I'm taking a moment to gather my thoughts, I don't want to give you the wrong impression. 

If I knew for absolutely certain that no one else could see it... I suppose I wouldn't be nearly as bothered. I mean, it's still there, and I know it's there, but... the worst part is the feeling that I'm making other people uncomfortable or that they're judging me for it. If I was just sitting alone in my house, well, it wouldn't matter much, would it? 

I really hope I'm explaining this right. I don't want you to think I'm completely vain or obsessed with myself. I just... I just don't want to be a bother to anyone else. Is that... does that sound like a normal way to feel about it?
Do you think you would still feel anxious about the scar if you were in a situation where you were completely alone?

Oh, I see... well, if I were completely alone... I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I'm sorry, I wish I had a better answer for you right away. 

I suppose if I'm just sitting by myself in the living room, reading a book or doing a crossword, I don't really think about it too much. It's not like I'm sitting there staring at my wrist all day when there's no one around. But... maybe sometimes, if I happen to catch a glimpse of it in the mirror or when I'm washing my hands, I might feel a little twinge of... well, just a little unhappy about it. But not really anxious, I don't think. 

It's really just the being around other people that gets me so worked up. I hope that makes sense? I'm trying to be as accurate as I can for you, I know you need the right details to help me. I'm doing okay with these questions, aren't I?
Do you think your anxiety about the scar would decrease if you were in a social situation where you felt completely accepted and liked by everyone around you?

Oh, that's... well, that's a lovely thought, isn't it? I'm sorry, I just had to imagine it for a second. 

If I were with people who I knew—really knew—liked me and accepted me just as I am... I'd like to think the anxiety would go away. Or at least, it would be much, much better. I mean, if I'm with my sister or my oldest friend, I don't tug at my sleeve quite as much. I still do a little bit, just out of habit, I suppose, because I don't want them to have to look at it either. But I don't get that awful tight feeling in my chest like I do when I'm at the grocery store or at the office. 

So, yes, I think it would decrease. I'm sorry, I hope I'm not making it sound like I only care about what strangers think of me. I just want to be presentable, you know? Does that sound like a reasonable way to react? I really do want to give you the right answers.
Do you think you would still feel anxious about the scar if everyone around you knew about it and had already accepted it?

Oh, goodness... if everyone already knew and had accepted it? I'm sorry, I'm having a little trouble picturing that, just because I usually try so hard to keep it covered up at the office. 

I suppose... well, I'm not entirely sure. If they really, truly didn't mind, maybe I wouldn't feel quite as on edge. But I think I'd still feel a bit... oh, I don't know, maybe just a little self-conscious? Just because I know it's not very nice to look at, and I wouldn't want to subject anyone to it even if they were polite about it. 

I've never really let it get to that point with people, so it's hard to say for certain. I'm sorry, I wish I could give you a more definite yes or no. Am I being too vague? I just want to make sure I'm answering you properly and giving you what you need.
Do you think you would feel anxious about the scar if you were in a situation where you were being evaluated or judged by others, but it had nothing to do with your appearance?

Oh, evaluated on something else... like an audit at work, or a performance review? I'm sorry, let me think about that for a second. 

I suppose... well, I really don't know for sure. I've never quite separated the two in my head. If my manager is looking over my ledgers, my main focus is definitely on making sure my numbers are perfect. But I think I'd still be a little careful to keep my sleeve pulled down, just so they wouldn't get distracted by the scar while we're going over the accounts. I just wouldn't want to seem unprofessional or messy. 

But I don't know if I'd call it being anxious about the scar in that moment, exactly. It's more just... wanting to make a good overall impression while they review my work? I'm sorry, I don't think I'm giving you a very clear answer here. It's just hard to imagine being evaluated and not worrying at least a tiny bit about looking tidy. Does that make sense for someone in my line of work? I really hope I'm not making this too complicated for you.
Do you think you would feel anxious about the scar if you were in a private setting where no one could see it, but you were still thinking about how others might perceive you if they were to see it?

Oh, if I'm completely alone... but just thinking about what others might think? I'm sorry, let me just think about that for a moment. 

Honestly, if I'm in my own home and no one is around, I don't really get that anxious feeling. I mean, I might think about it briefly if I'm getting dressed or washing up, but I don't just sit and worry about imaginary people looking at me. I try to keep myself busy with my reading or my chores, you know? 

I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around obsessing over it all hours of the day, because I'm really not. It's mostly just when I'm out and about and want to make sure I look tidy for other people. I hope that's okay to say? I just want to be completely honest with you so you have the right information. Does that sound like a typical way to handle it?
Do you think your anxiety about the scar would decrease if you knew that everyone around you had seen it and thought it was a normal part of who you are?

Oh, goodness... if everyone already knew and just thought it was normal? I'm sorry, I'm trying to picture that. 

I suppose... well, maybe? If they really, truly didn't mind and just saw it as part of me, I might feel a little less worried about making sure my sleeves are pulled down just right. But honestly, I'm not entirely sure. I think I'd still want to keep it covered, just to be polite. I wouldn't want to make anyone uncomfortable, even if they said they were fine with it. It's just about being presentable, you know?

I'm sorry, I know that's not a very helpful answer. It's just so hard to imagine a situation like that because I've always been so careful to keep it neat and out of sight. I hope I'm not being too difficult? I really want to give you the answers you're looking for, I just don't know if I'd ever feel completely relaxed about it, even then. Does that make sense?
Do you think your anxiety about the scar is mostly because you fear being judged or evaluated negatively by others when they see it?

Oh, judged or evaluated negatively... I'm sorry, I just want to make sure I'm understanding you correctly. 

I wouldn't say I'm terrified of being judged, exactly. I don't want to make it sound like I'm paranoid or anything like that, because I'm really not. It's more just... well, in my line of work, being neat and presentable is so important. When people see something that looks a bit messy or out of place, like my scar, they might just think I'm careless. And I would hate for anyone to think I'm not taking my job or myself seriously. 

So I suppose I do worry a little bit about what they might think, but mostly just because I want to be polite and professional. I just want to make a good impression, like anyone else would. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I'm sorry if I'm not explaining it very well. I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need for your notes. Is it normal to just want to look tidy?
Do you think you would still feel anxious about the scar if you knew that everyone around you accepted and liked you, not despite the scar, but because of who you are as a person?

Oh, goodness... if everyone accepted me and liked me because of who I am? I'm sorry, that's a very kind thought. Let me just think about that for a second.

I suppose... well, if I knew they truly liked me for me, I might feel a little more at ease. But honestly, I think I'd still want to keep it covered up. It's not that I don't believe them, or that I think they're lying... it's just that I'd still feel a bit untidy. I've been a bookkeeper for so long, and everything always has to be just so, you know? Neat columns, everything balancing out perfectly. 

I just wouldn't want to present myself in a way that looks messy, even to people who care about me. I'd still feel like I wasn't putting my best foot forward. I hope I don't sound ungrateful or... or stubborn by saying that. I just really value looking put-together. Does that make sense? I'm sorry, I hope I'm answering this the way you need me to.
Do you think you would still feel anxious about the scar if you were certain that everyone around you viewed it as a normal and acceptable part of your appearance?

Oh, dear... I feel like I might be frustrating you, since this sounds so similar to what you just asked. I must not have given you a very good answer a moment ago, and I am so sorry about that. Let me try to think about it a little harder. 

If I knew for absolute certain that everyone thought it was completely acceptable... well, I honestly just don't know if I can say for sure. It's so hard to picture a situation like that. I think I would probably still feel a little unsettled, just because *I* know it's there, and it still wouldn't look quite right to me in the mirror. It's hard to turn off that feeling of wanting things to look proper. 

But maybe... maybe the worry wouldn't be quite as heavy? If I knew nobody else minded, I might not check my sleeves quite as often. I really hope that's a better answer for you? I'm trying my very best to think about it exactly the way you're asking, I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your wrist for any other reasons besides the scar?

Oh, no, no, it's really just the scar. I hope I didn't make it sound like I'm constantly staring at my wrist for no reason! I just... well, before I leave the house, I might just glance at it in the hall mirror a few times. Just to make sure everything looks tidy. 

Sometimes I'll try on a different sleeve length, or maybe slip on a bracelet, just to see what covers it best. And occasionally I'll ask my husband if it looks obvious. He always says it's barely there, bless his heart, but I just like to be sure. It's just a little morning routine to make sure I'm put-together before I head out. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
